slides.title: Your best niche is [already in your invoices].
slides.lede: Most established firms already hold the evidence. What fails is that nobody outside the firm can see it.

slides.title: Mine [three years] of engagements first
slides.text: Sort the work by sector, service line and client type. Rank each segment on fee income, realisation, repeat or referred work, and how much the team enjoys it.

slides.title: What a niche needs [before any marketing]

items.title: Capability
items.text: People and capacity to serve it well.

items.title: Concentration
items.text: A meaningful share of fees or referrals.

items.title: Willingness to refuse
items.text: Partners decline work that conflicts with it.

slides.title: Being the specialist and [looking like one]

cards.label: Capability
cards.text: What the firm can actually do.

cards.label: Position
cards.text: What a buyer believes before any conversation.

slides.title: Ask a stranger [in your target segment]
slides.note: If the answer is vague, you have **capability without position**.

slides.title: Partners agree on [evidence, not principle]
slides.text: Ask three questions in order: which segment earns the highest realisation, which refers new work, and which can we serve better than any competitor?

slides.title: Choose the niche your evidence supports.
slides.lede: Six steps to choose a niche, get partners to agree and make the market see it. Read the full guide via the link in our bio.
